title: Balanced Meal
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use the meals children eat: ugali, sukuma and beans; githeri; rice and stew; chapati and ndengu. A balanced meal can be cheap.

skills.key_step: The child explains that a balanced meal gives the body energy, growth and protection from disease, keeps a person healthy and strong, and need not be expensive.

floor.prerequisite: Knows foods are put in groups.
floor.question: Name a food that gives energy.

representations: a plate chart with three parts
a story of a child who eats only ugali
steps: Energy foods: to work and play.
Body-building foods: to grow and repair.
All three every meal: healthy and strong.
contexts: a school lunch of githeri and greens
a family meal on a market day

board.do: Draw a plate cut into three parts.

board.say: What happens if we never eat protective food?

listen_for: It is big enough to fill the stomach
misconceptions.repair: Compare a large plate of ugali alone with a smaller plate of ugali, beans and greens.

listen_for: Ugali gives everything the body needs
misconceptions.ask: Why can a child not live on ugali alone?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to a child who eats only one food for months.

listen_for: Only a rich family that can buy meat
misconceptions.ask: Which family can eat a balanced meal?
misconceptions.repair: Make a cheap balanced meal with ugali, ndengu and managu.

listen_for: A very big plate of food
misconceptions.repair: Show a big plate of only rice next to a smaller plate of rice, beans and cabbage; ask which has all three groups.

checks.question: Why should we eat a balanced meal?
checks.answer: to stay healthy, grow and have energy

checks.question: Does a balanced meal need costly food?
checks.answer: no, local foods like githeri and greens balance a meal

skills.key_step: The child sorts foods into energy-giving (ugali, rice, potatoes, bread, fats), body-building (beans, meat, eggs, fish, milk, ndengu) and protective (vegetables and fruits).

floor.prerequisite: Knows the three jobs of food in the body.
floor.question: What do body-building foods do?

representations: real foods or pictures to sort
steps: Ask: does it give energy, build the body or protect?

board.do: Draw three columns: energy, body-building, protective.

misconceptions.repair: Ask what a runner eats before a race and why.

misconceptions.ask: Eggs, fish and beans help the body to do what mainly?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which foods a growing child or someone with a wound needs.

misconceptions.ask: Sukuma wiki and mangoes are which kind of food?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what protective means and which colours protect the body.
Ask what young animals and babies grow on; milk builds the body.

checks.question: Which group is an egg in?
Which group is an orange in?

skills.key_step: The child picks or builds a meal with at least one food from each group and says which food is from which group.

floor.prerequisite: Can sort foods into the three groups.
floor.question: Which group is sukuma wiki in?

representations: a tick chart for the three groups
steps: List the foods on the plate.
If a group is empty, add a food from it.

board.do: Write "rice and chicken" on a plate.

misconceptions.ask: Which plate is a balanced meal?
misconceptions.repair: Sort each food on the plate into a group. Count the groups.

misconceptions.ask: A child eats ugali and fish. What is missing?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which group each food is in and which group is empty.

misconceptions.ask: Which one makes a meal more balanced?
misconceptions.repair: Look at what a soda gives: sugar and no body-building or protective foods.
Tick the groups on a plate chart: energy, body-building, protective. One box stays empty.

checks.question: Make ugali and fish a balanced meal.
Is chapati, rice and bread balanced?
checks.answer: no, all three are energy foods
